articles.title: British MPs urge government to block UAE's Nusseibeh from top UN job
articles.summary:
British MPs urge government to block UAE's Nusseibeh from top UN job

Submitted by Oscar Rickett on Tue, 11/17/2026 - 13:41
Emirati diplomat has 'repeatedly denied and dismissed' UN reports on Sudan, MPs from across the political spectrum tell Ed Miliband
UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh at the United Nations headquarters in New York City, last month (David Delgado/Reuters)
Off

Sixty-six British MPs from across the political spectrum have called on their government to use its veto as a permanent member of the UN Security Council to stop the UAE’s Lana Nusseibeh from becoming the world body’s next secretary general.

In a letter to Ed Miliband, the UK’s foreign secretary, Liberal Democrat MP Monica Harding writes that Nusseibeh is “not a credible candidate” for the role because she has “repeatedly denied and dismissed” reports by the UN Panel of Experts and other groups linking the UAE to the war in Sudan.

A recent confidential quarterly report from the UN Panel of Experts on Sudan, which was obtained by Middle East Eye, established conclusively that the UAE had hired Colombian mercenaries to fight for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the Sudanese paramilitary group that the UN and US determined has committed genocide in Darfur.

The UAE has armed and equipped the RSF using supply lines that run through Libya, Chad, Ethiopia and the breakaway Somali regions of Puntland and Somaliland. Abu Dhabi continues to deny the charges.

Nusseibeh, an Emirati diplomat of Palestinian descent, is one of eight candidates seeking to succeed Antonio Guterres, whose term ends on 31 December.

MEE understands that the Security Council’s next straw poll - an informal, anonymous poll on whether members encourage, discourage or have no opinion about a candidate - will take place on Thursday. 

Furthermore, diplomatic and humanitarian sources believe that Nusseibeh now has the backing of all five of the Security Council’s permanent members - the US, UK, France, China and Russia - which are the only countries that can veto candidates. 

The UAE in Sudan

The Emirati diplomat’s candidacy has been particularly controversial because of her country’s involvement in wars in Sudan, Yemen and Libya, and because Abu Dhabi is Israel’s key ally in the region. 

In September 2024, months after a UN panel of experts had set out a credible case that the UAE was arming the RSF, Nusseibeh wrote to the Economist under her own name and said it was not true. The Emirates, she wrote, had supplied no weapons at all. 

A year after that letter, sources in the European Parliament said that Nusseibeh, who was the UAE’s ambassador to the UN from 2013 to 2024, went to Strasbourg and lobbied it to remove the words “United Arab Emirates” from a resolution on what was being done in Sudan.   

'Lady Macbeth thought a little water clears her of these deeds. Abu Dhabi now seems to believe the UN’s blue flag can do the same'

- Amgad Fareid Eltayeb, Sudanese government adviser

“Lady Macbeth thought ‘a little water clears her of these deeds’. Abu Dhabi now seems to believe the UN’s blue flag can do the same,” Amgad Fareid Eltayeb, a Sudanese government adviser, told MEE.

“Lana Nusseibeh disputed UN findings on Emirati support for the RSF, now her government wants her to lead the institution whose findings she rejected. How can she credibly promise independence from the government helping finance her campaign?”

In a recent interview with the Financial Times, Nusseibeh said that ending the war in Sudan, which began in April 2023 between the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces, would be her most urgent focus. 

“There's nobody who doesn't come from somewhere,” she said, when asked how she could uphold international humanitarian law after representing a government accused of violating it.

'Nusseibeh is not a credible candidate'

Harding’s letter to Ed Miliband begins by saying that at a time when the world is “more uncertain” than it has been in decades, “the importance of the United Nations - the ultimate expression of multilateralism - is greater than ever…”

“It is therefore with concern that we note that Lana Nusseibeh, a diplomat from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has entered the race at this late stage. Ms Nusseibeh is not a credible candidate,” Harding writes.

Leaked UN report 'establishes conclusively' that UAE hired Colombian mercenaries for Sudan's RSF
Read More »

The letter is signed by MPs from the Liberal Democrats, Greens, Conservatives, Scottish National Party, Your Party and the governing Labour Party. 

“The war in Sudan has led to the world's largest humanitarian catastrophe. Ms Nusseibeh has dismissed the findings of the UN’s Panel of Experts on Sudan which described as ‘credible’ allegations that the UAE was arming the RSF,” the letter reads.

“Despite numerous and credible reports of the UAE's support to the Rapid Support Forces, which have been accused of 'war crimes, crimes against humanity and conduct displaying hallmarks of genocide', Ms Nusseibeh has repeatedly denied and dismissed this.”

The letter concludes by calling “on the government to use its position as a Permanent Member of the UN Security Council to block Ms Nusseibeh’s candidacy and allow a candidate to take on the role who is better placed to facilitate peace in the world’s worst humanitarian crisis and stand up for the values of the United Nations”.

Pressure on the UK

Sources familiar with the British government’s thinking have told MEE that the UK is backing Nusseibeh’s candidacy and will not use its veto to block her. 

One former British diplomat told MEE that Nusseibeh, who was educated in England and was instrumental to the UAE’s normalisation of relations with Israel in 2020, is thought of very highly. 

'They're a selfish bunch': How Abu Dhabi shaped modern Manchester
Read More »

“She’s charming. She’s extremely eloquent. She’s a fast thinker. She’s the best diplomat I’ve ever met,” the source said. “She’s assertive, and so she’s been good at articulating the UAE’s foreign policy position, which is that it has a right to be assertive.”

The UAE has poured billions of pounds into the UK, where its vice president, Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, owns Manchester City Football Club, as well as a significant chunk of Manchester itself. The city’s former mayor, Andy Burnham, is now the UK’s prime minister.

The Foreign Office has said it will not publicly comment on individual candidates. “The UK’s priority is to find the candidate best equipped to lead the UN in tackling our shared global challenges,” a spokesperson told MEE on 6 November.

“Our focus is on the merit of the candidates to secure the most qualified candidate for the next UN secretary general.”

UK Politics
Imran Mulla
London

articles.title: Crew abandon gas tanker off Hormuz after being hit by projectile, sources say
articles.summary:
Crew abandon gas tanker off Hormuz after being hit by projectile, sources say

The crew of a liquefied petroleum gas tanker abandoned ship on Tuesday after the vessel was struck by a projectile while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, maritime security sources said.

The crew of the Panama-flagged Tara Gas LPG tanker abandoned ship around 7 nautical miles (13 km) off Oman's Khasab coast, the sources said, and one crew member remains missing.

The vessel's Marshall Islands-based owner, listed in databases as Global Gas, could not be reached for comment.

The vessel last reported its position on September 26 off Oman's coast, according to ship tracking data on the MarineTraffic platform.

Earlier on Tuesday, British navy linked agency UKMTO said the crew of a tanker passing through the Strait of Hormuz was unaccounted for after it was attacked for a second time north of the port city of Khasab in Oman. It gave no further details.

Reporting by Reuters

articles.title: Bahraini activist Nabeel Rajab dies in Turkey
articles.summary:
Bahraini activist Nabeel Rajab dies in Turkey

Submitted by Areeb Ullah on Tue, 11/17/2026 - 12:58
Rajab, who campaigned for human rights in Bahrain and the Gulf, died on Tuesday at the age of 62
Nabeel Rajab was found unresponsive at his home in Turkey by his wife and daughter after fleeing Bahrain earlier this year over fears of re-arrest (AFP)
Off

Bahraini human rights activist Nabeel Rajab died on Tuesday in Turkey at the age of 62. Fellow campaigners said he died after suffering a heart attack.

Ebrahim Sharif, an activist who was a close friend of the family, told the Associated Press that Rajab’s wife and daughter found him unresponsive early in the morning at their home in Turkey. 

Reflecting on the activist's life, Sayed Ahmed al-Wadaei, advocacy director at the London-based Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy, described him as a "beautiful soul" who was "as noble as his name [Nabeel]".

"Nabeel defended our rights with dignity and paid a heavy personal price, as did his family, for standing up for the rights of his people," Wadaei wrote on X.

"He suffered imprisonment and abuse by the state for exposing human rights violations. He left Bahrain after witnessing the body of Sayed Mohamed Almousawi, who was murdered under torture."

Rajab left Bahrain early in the Iran war and fled to Turkey after fearing he would be imprisoned again by Bahrain for releasing a statement accusing the government of the death of Almousawi, a former political prisoner. 

Rajab, who became one of the most recognisable figures of the country’s pro-democracy movement, spent much of his adult life challenging the authorities over political repression, torture and restrictions on freedom of expression.

Nabeel Rajab: A true patriot's journey
Read More »

As president of the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights (BCHR), Rajab helped bring international attention to abuses in the Gulf kingdom, documenting violations and campaigning for the release of political prisoners.

His activism made him a frequent target of the Bahraini authorities, who repeatedly arrested and prosecuted him over his participation in demonstrations and his criticism of the government.

He was released from prison in 2020 while serving a five year prison term for his activism into a non-custodial sentence.

Rajab was among the most prominent activists to emerge from the 2011 uprising in Bahrain, when thousands of demonstrators took to the streets demanding political reform, greater accountability and an end to discrimination.

His campaigning extended beyond Bahrain’s borders, with Rajab criticising western governments and regional allies for supporting the Bahraini authorities.

In 2015, Rajab spoke to Middle East Eye after coming out of prison, and said the tide was slowly changing with internationational partners acknowledging that "Bahrain is a dictatorship that marginalises and discriminates against its indigenous population". 

"Before, nobody talked about Bahrain, but today [in 2015] 47 Western countries are criticising Bahrain's human rights record, and today you see awareness among people, among media, which never existed," he said. 

From rights campaigning to the streets

Born in Bahrain on 1 September 1964, Rajab studied political science and history at the University of Pune in India and graduated in 1987.

He became involved in human rights activism during the 1990s, a period of political unrest in Bahrain, and later helped establish several civil society organisations.

Among them was the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights, founded in 2002, which documented allegations of torture, arbitrary detention and restrictions on civil liberties.

The Bahraini authorities dissolved the organisation in 2004, but it continued its work despite the ban.

Rajab later became its president and helped establish the Gulf Centre for Human Rights, expanding his work to document abuses across the region.

His activism covered a wide range of issues, including the treatment of migrant workers, political prisoners, freedom of speech and the rights of people detained by the United States at Guantanamo Bay.

He grew more prominent as social media enabled activists to communicate directly with international audiences.

The 2011 uprising

Rajab emerged as a leading figure during Bahrain’s 2011 pro-democracy uprising, which began in February that year as protests swept across the Arab world.

Demonstrators gathered at the Pearl Roundabout in the capital, Manama, demanding political reforms and an end to discrimination and repression.

Rights groups condemn Bahrain's largest mass trial of Shia clerics in history
Read More »

The authorities responded with a violent crackdown. In March 2011, troops from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates entered Bahrain as part of a Gulf Cooperation Council deployment, helping the government suppress the protests.

Rajab documented the crackdown and became a prominent voice in the international campaign to hold the Bahraini authorities accountable.

He criticised the arrests of opposition figures, the treatment of detainees and the use of force against demonstrators.

His work also put him at odds with Bahrain’s regional allies, particularly Saudi Arabia, whose military intervention he opposed.

The authorities increasingly targeted Rajab through arrests, prosecutions and travel restrictions.

In May 2012, he was detained for criticising the interior ministry for failing to investigate attacks by pro-government armed gangs against Shia residents. He was subsequently convicted of insulting a public institution.

In August that year, he received a three-year prison sentence for his involvement in protests and demonstrations. The sentence was later reduced to two years on appeal.

His detention drew international condemnation, with human rights organisations arguing that he was being punished for exercising his rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly.

After his release in May 2014, Rajab continued to criticise the government.

He was arrested again in October that year over social media posts criticising the interior and defence ministries.

He was later released on medical grounds in July 2015, but remained subject to restrictions on his freedom of movement.

In June 2016, he was arrested once more, this time over comments about Bahrain’s participation in the Saudi-led military campaign in Yemen and allegations of torture inside Jaw Prison.

In February 2018, a Bahraini court sentenced him to five years in prison for what prosecutors described as spreading false news and insulting state institutions.

The case drew widespread criticism from international human rights groups and United Nations experts.

During his imprisonment, concerns were repeatedly raised about Rajab's health and treatment, especially prolonged solitary confinement and poor prison conditions.

Human Rights Watch reported that he was held in a cramped and unhygienic cell for extended periods. He was released in 2020.

Inside Bahrain

Rostoucí obavy z eskalace podtrhují incidenty v Hormuzském průlivu a přetrvávající asymetrická hrozba pro globální námořní trasy.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and Red Sea remains highly tense due to ongoing Houthi attacks, which recently struck a key Aramco building in the Saudi capital. Growing fears of escalation are underscored by incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and the persistent asymmetric threat to global shipping lanes.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zvýšenou volatilitu cen ropy a komodit v reakci na přetrvávající útoky v oblasti Perského zálivu a Rudého moře, přičemž investoři budou nadále bedlivě sledovat jakékoliv náznaky vojenské či diplomatické eskalace.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, increased volatility in oil and commodity prices is expected in response to ongoing attacks in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea, while investors will closely monitor any signs of military or diplomatic escalation.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Perského zálivu zůstává kritická kvůli probíhajícím útokům na ropné tankery a infrastrukturu, včetně nedávného úderu na budovu Aramco v Rijádu ze strany Houthiů. Uzavřený Hormuzský průliv a přetrvávající napětí mezi USA a Íránem drží globální trhy v pohotovosti navzdory mírnému nárůstu dodávek.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and Persian Gulf remains critical due to ongoing attacks on oil tankers and infrastructure, including a recent strike by Houthis on the Aramco building in Riyadh. The closed Strait of Hormuz and persistent US-Iran tensions keep global markets on high alert despite a slight recovery in oil flows.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat přetrvávající vysokou volatilitu cen komodit a ropy, podpořenou novými útoky Houthiů a napětím v oblasti Perského zálivu. Trhy budou nadále citlivě reagovat na jakékoliv zprávy o vojenské eskalaci.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued high volatility in commodity and oil prices is expected, driven by fresh Houthi attacks and ongoing tensions in the Persian Gulf. Markets will remain highly sensitive to any news regarding military escalation.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu zůstává kritická, což dokládají nedávné útoky Houthiů na energetickou infrastrukturu v Saúdské Arábii a přetrvávající napadení tankerů v Hormuzském průlivu. Hrozby odvetných kroků ze strany Íránu a incidenty spojené s kybernetickou bezpečností nadále narušují stabilitu mezinárodního obchodu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East remains critical, highlighted by recent Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and ongoing strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian retaliation threats and cybersecurity incidents continue to disrupt international trade stability.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat přetrvávající vysokou volatilitu cen komodit a ropy kvůli nezmenšenému napětí v Perském zálivu a útokům na infrastrukturu. Finanční trhy budou extrémně citlivě reagovat na jakékoliv zprávy o vojenské odvetě.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, high volatility in commodity and oil prices is expected to persist due to unabated tensions in the Persian Gulf and infrastructure attacks. Financial markets will remain extremely sensitive to any news regarding military retaliation.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a námořních tras zůstává kritická, což potvrzují nedávné útoky na energetickou infrastrukturu a ropné tankery v regionu. Houtiové pokračují v útocích, přičemž nejnovější zásahy v saúdském hlavním městě podtrhují přetrvávající rizika pro globální logistiku a dodávky energií.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and maritime corridors remains critical, underscored by recent attacks on energy infrastructure and oil tankers in the region. The Houthis continue their strikes, with the latest hits in the Saudi capital highlighting persistent risks to global logistics and energy supplies.
archive.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech lze očekávat zvýšenou volatilitu na energetických trzích a pokračující bezpečnostní opatření v námořní dopravě. Jakékoliv nové zprávy o eskalaci v Perském zálivu okamžitě ovlivní ceny ropy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened volatility in energy markets and ongoing security measures in maritime shipping are expected. Any fresh news of escalation in the Persian Gulf will immediately impact oil prices.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a Perského zálivu zůstává napjatá kvůli pokračujícím útokům na ropné tankery a vojenská zařízení. Růst hrozeb pro námořní dopravu nadále vynucuje přísná bezpečnostní opatření a prodlužování tras lodí mimo rizikové oblasti.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and the Persian Gulf remains tense due to ongoing attacks on oil tankers and military installations. Heightened threats to maritime shipping continue to necessitate strict security measures and the rerouting of vessels away from high-risk zones.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat přetrvávající volatilitu na komoditních trzích a opatrnost investorů kvůli rizikům další eskalace v oblasti Perského zálivu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, persistent volatility in commodity markets and investor caution due to risks of further escalation in the Persian Gulf region are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a Perského zálivu prudce eskaluje po sérii útoků na námořní dopravu, včetně minového incidentu v Hormuzském průlivu a úderů na vojenská zařízení. Rizika pro komerční plavbu a energetické koridory zůstávají na kritické úrovni.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Middle East and Persian Gulf is escalating sharply following a series of attacks on maritime traffic, including a naval mine incident in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on military installations. Risks to commercial shipping and energy corridors remain at a critical level.
archive.forecast_cs: V příštích dnech lze očekávat vysokou volatilitu cen ropy a přetrvávající opatrnost investorů kvůli reálnému riziku další ozbrojené eskalace v oblasti Perského zálivu.
archive.forecast_en: High volatility in oil prices and persistent investor caution are expected over the coming days due to the tangible risk of further armed escalation in the Persian Gulf.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Perského zálivu a Hormuzského průlivu zůstává vysoce nestabilní kvůli opakovaným útokům na tankery a námořním minám. Navzdory částečnému oživení exportu ropy přetrvávají přímé hrozby pro globální námořní dopravu a bezpečnost posádek.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz remains highly volatile due to repeated tanker attacks and naval mines. Despite a partial recovery in oil exports, direct threats to global maritime shipping and crew safety persist.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující volatilitu cen komodit a napětí kolem námořních tras v důsledku přetrvávajících vojenských incidentů.
archive.forecast_en: Continued volatility in commodity prices and tension around shipping lanes are expected over the coming days due to ongoing military incidents.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Perského zálivu a Hormuzského průlivu zůstává kritická kvůli pokračujícím útokům na tankery, námořním minám a přímým vojenským incidentům mezi USA a Iránem. Provoz v klíčových námořních trasách je nadále silně narušen, což generuje enormní tlak na globální dodavatelské řetězce.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz remains critical due to ongoing tanker attacks, naval mines, and direct military incidents between the US and Iran. Traffic in key maritime routes continues to be severely disrupted, generating enormous pressure on global supply chains.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat vysokou volatilitu na energetických trzích a přetrvávající bezpečnostní opatření kolem strategických úžin vlivem přímých konfrontací.
archive.forecast_en: High volatility in energy markets and persistent security measures around strategic straits are expected over the coming days due to direct confrontations.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a Rudého moře zůstává vysoce napjatá kvůli nedávným přímým útokům íránských Revolučních gard (IRGC) na americkou základnu v Bahrajnu a aktivitám Houthiů. Konflikt nadále narušuje námořní trasy, vyvolává obavy z uzavření klíčových úžin a nutí přepravce k prodlužování tras.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and Red Sea remains highly tense due to recent direct attacks by Iran's IRGC on a US base in Bahrain and Houthi activities. The conflict continues to disrupt maritime routes, raise concerns over the closure of strategic straits, and force shippers to take longer detours.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zvýšenou volatilitu na energetických trzích a přetrvávající bezpečnostní opatření v oblasti Perského zálivu a Rudého moře kvůli eskalaci útoků. Diplomatické snahy budou pod silným tlakem vzhledem k vojenským odvetným akcím.
archive.forecast_en: High volatility in energy markets and persistent security measures across the Persian Gulf and Red Sea are expected over the coming days due to escalating attacks. Diplomatic efforts will remain under severe pressure amid military retaliations.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Perského zálivu a Blízkého východu eskaluje po přímých útocích na americké vojenské radary a infrastrukturu v Bahrajnu. Námořní doprava čelí hrozbám nejen v Rudém moři, ale nově i v Hormuzském průlivu, kde došlo k zasažení ropného tankeru námořní minou.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Persian Gulf and Middle East has escalated sharply following direct attacks on US military radar and infrastructure in Bahrain. Maritime trade faces severe threats not only in the Red Sea but increasingly in the Strait of Hormuz, where an oil tanker was struck by a naval mine.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující volatilitu na energetických trzích a zvýšené napětí v Perském zálivu i Rudém moři v důsledku eskalujících útoků na vojenskou a námořní infrastrukturu.
archive.forecast_en: Continued volatility in energy markets and elevated tensions in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea are expected over the coming days as attacks on military and maritime infrastructure escalate.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává kritická kvůli přímým útokům na americké základny v Bahrajnu, minovým incidentům v Hormuzském průlivu a aktivitě Houthiů v oblasti Rudého moře. Přítomnost tří amerických úderných skupin letadlových lodí odráží extrémní stupeň eskalace konfliktu.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation remains critical due to direct attacks on US bases in Bahrain, mine incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi activity in the Red Sea region. The presence of three US carrier strike groups reflects an extreme level of conflict escalation.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat vysokou nervozitu na energetických trzích a pokračující vojenské manévry v Perském zálivu i Rudém moři. Riziko dalšího přímého střetu zůstává akutní.
archive.forecast_en: High nervousness in energy markets and ongoing military maneuvers in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea are expected over the coming days. The risk of further direct confrontation remains acute.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Perského zálivu eskaluje po útocích na ropné tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a přímých dronech na americkou základnu v Bahrajnu. Jemnští Hútiové navíc postupují blíže k Adenu v návaznosti na stahování vládních sil z oblasti Bab al-Mandebu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and Persian Gulf is escalating following naval mine strikes on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and drone attacks on a US military base in Bahrain. Furthermore, Houthi forces are pushing closer to Aden following the withdrawal of government troops from the Bab al-Mandeb area.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další testování americké přítomnosti v regionu, vysokou volatilitu cen ropy a přetrvávající bezpečnostní opatření kolem námořních tras.
archive.forecast_en: Further testing of the US regional presence, high volatility in oil prices, and persistent security measures around maritime routes are expected over the coming days.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a námořních koridorů se nadále vyhsoce eskaluje v důsledku přímých útoků na tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a úderů na americké základny v Bahrajnu. Houtiové mezitím postupují v Jemenu, což ohrožuje klíčový průliv Bab al-Mandab a celkovou svobodu globální plavby navzdory masivnímu nasazení tří amerických letadlových lodí.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and maritime corridors continues to escalate severely due to direct attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on US bases in Bahrain. Meanwhile, Houthi forces are advancing in Yemen, threatening the critical Bab al-Mandab strait and overall freedom of global navigation despite the massive deployment of three US aircraft carriers.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat stupňování vojenských operací v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu a Jemenu, což povede k další volatilitě cen ropy a přetrvávajícím bezpečnostním opatřením.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, an escalation of military operations in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen is expected, leading to further oil price volatility and persistent security measures.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu, Rudého moře a přilehlých vodních cest se dramaticky zostřuje v důsledku útoků na tankery, námořních min a rozsáhlých vojenských operací USA a jejich spojenců. Postup Houthiů v Jemenu a eskalace napětí s Iránem nadále ohrožují klíčové globální námořní trasy a energetickou infrastrukturu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and surrounding waterways is sharply deteriorating due to tanker attacks, naval mines, and extensive military operations by the US and its allies. Houthi advances in Yemen and escalating tensions with Iran continue to threaten critical global shipping lanes and energy infrastructure.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další eskalaci vojenských střetů v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu a Jemenu, což udrží ceny energií a volatilitu na vysokých úrovních.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of military clashes in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen is expected, keeping energy prices and volatility elevated.
